subject: Programmatic opt-out: SDK hooks, evidence pack, and rollout plan
messages:
From: Leo Park <leo@nimblehealth.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karen Li <legal@nimblehealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Programmatic opt-out + evidence we can rely on

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal raised two items we need before we can sign:

1) A programmatic opt-out mechanism (SDK + API) that allows tenant-level and per-request no-train flags. We need a clear developer integration pattern (client SDK header, server-side enforcement, and fallback behavior).
2) Concrete evidence we can hand to our compliance team showing requests tagged with no-train are excluded from all model-improvement pipelines and not used to fine-tune or eval.

Attached is a short spec (nimble_spec_request.pdf) showing what we mean. Can Redwood provide a technical design + a short evidence pack (logs, retention policy snapshot, and a statement of adherence) by next week?

Scope: this will cover both streaming and batch ingestion from our platform, and it needs to work with Dedicated or Hosted deployments.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if needed.

—Leo Park
Principal Engineer, NimbleHealth
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Leo Park <leo@nimblehealth.ai>

Leo / Karen —

Appreciate the level of detail — this is very actionable. Quick plan and asks from our side:

- Deliverables (target by Nov 30):
  • Implementation design doc for SDK hooks and API header (we’ll show header name, server enforcement, and fallback semantics).
  • Evidence pack outline (what we can produce for Hosted vs Dedicated: retention policy screenshots, request routing logs, and a signed statement from our Privacy team).
- Owners: Marcus will draft the design; David will own the evidence pack and legal statement. I’ll coordinate timelines and be your primary contact.
- Open questions for Nimble: do you need tenant-level default = no-train (true) or per-request opt-out only? Also, what SLA for evidence delivery is acceptable — e.g., redacted logs vs full request captures?

If that works I’ll route the internal PRD and schedule a short sync for Thursday to confirm edge cases (streaming + partial-response caching).

Thanks,
Stephanie

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Leo Park <leo@nimblehealth.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Karen Li <legal@nimblehealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Programmatic opt-out + evidence we can rely on

Hi all —

Draft technical approach (summary):

- Client integration: SDKs (Python/Node/Java) will expose a boolean flag on the request call: no_train=true. For REST/HTTP integrations we will accept an explicit header: X-Redwood-No-Train: 1 (values: 0/1).

- Server enforcement: the routing layer will mark the request as NO_TRAIN and set an immutable attribute on the request record. That attribute is used by downstream subsystems (telemetry, training pipeline, eval ingestion) to filter out requests. We’ll add an additional check in the model improvement ingestion step to drop any record (or derivative) tied to requests with NO_TRAIN.

- Caching and KV: for low-latency workloads we will continue to use ephemeral KV caches for active sessions, but NO_TRAIN requests will be stored only in ephemeral memory and will not land on disk-backed caches or persistent traces. Ephemeral tokens are scrubbed on session termination.

- Logs & evidence: we can produce redacted request logs showing the header + timestamp + tenant id + routing decision. For Hosted customers we can produce a signed CSV snapshot (no prompt text) and for Dedicated we can validate locally-run ingestion configs and provide a signed operational attestation.

- Edge cases: streaming chunks will inherit the parent request flag. Retries and augmentation flows will propagate NO_TRAIN; if a client omits the header on a retry it will be recorded as NO_TRAIN=false and treated separately (we will surface retries in the evidence pack).

Next steps I’ll deliver: a one-page design (attached: redwood_no_train_design.pdf) and a short runbook for operations to generate the evidence snapshot.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Product Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karen Li <legal@nimblehealth.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Leo Park <leo@nimblehealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Programmatic opt-out + evidence we can rely on

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from the legal/compliance side before we finalize the DPA redline: 

1) Evidence scope: we need a deliverable that shows a complete request lineage for a sampling window (7 days) that includes: tenant id, timestamp, NO_TRAIN flag, routing decision, and confirmation that the request did not enter any model improvement queues. Redacted prompt text is OK.
2) Attestation: can Redwood provide an operations attestation signed by your Head of Security/Privacy confirming controls are in place and periodically audited?
3) Exportability: if we move from Hosted -> Dedicated in future, what artifacts will we get to validate the same behavior?

If you can provide a short evidence pack and the attestation, legal is comfortable adding a narrowly scoped no-training commitment into the DPA (we’ll share proposed language). We’d prefer the evidence snapshot by next Wednesday (Dec 2).

—Karen Li
Lead Counsel, NimbleHealth
